findings.statement: The initiating event was the lightning trip of the Blyth–Eccles–Stella West 400 kV circuit at 16:50:44 BST, which started the loss of generation.
The ESO's technical report (Table 2) gives the total generation lost as 1,990 MW.
Ofgem reports that LFDD disconnected 931 MW of demand.
The DNOs reported 892 MW of demand disconnected by LFDD relays.
In total 1,462 MW of distributed generation was lost on loss-of-mains protection: 150 MW + 350 MW + 500 MW + 462 MW = 1,462 MW.
Adding the ESO's 1,878 MW, the further 200 MW at 49 Hz and the 550 MW lost with LFDD gives 1,878 MW + 200 MW + 550 MW = 2,628 MW of generation lost.
The ESO's technical report (Table 3) gives 1,338 MW of secondary response held.
ESO Table 4 gives system inertia of 219,632 MVA.s on 9 August.
The root cause of the ST1C trip was a faulty speed sensor, and GT1A tripped because a bypass valve failed to open.
GT1B tripped automatically on high steam pressure, as recorded in the ESO control log entry S07-E14.
The Dynamic Reactive Compensator failed and caused the Hornsea One de-load.
The frequency minimum was 48.8 Hz at 16:53:49 BST.
The first post-fault minimum was 49.1 Hz at 16:52:58 BST.
Frequency was below 49 Hz for 40 s.
All demand was restored at 18:34 BST.
In January 2020 Ofgem announced that RWE and Ørsted each agreed to make voluntary payments of £4.5m to the redress scheme, and that EPN and SPN paid £1.5m.
Ofgem found that Hornsea One breached its licence and was found to be in breach of the Grid Code.
29 Class 700 and 717 trains were locked out: 27 were reset by their drivers and 30 needed a technician to attend on site.
Two Class 387 trains also shut down when the frequency fell below 49 Hz.
Units on software 3.25.x went into a permanent lock-out needing a technician, while units on 3.27.x could be reset by drivers.
The Thameslink Class 700 trains stopped because their overhead-line traction supply was lost when LFDD disconnected the railway.
The Class 700 and 717 protection tripped at 48.8 Hz.
Rail services suffered 873 delay minutes.
Newcastle Airport lost supply when its own site protection systems tripped.
Ipswich Hospital was disconnected by the LFDD scheme.
An oil refinery was disconnected by LFDD, and the Stanlow refinery flared when its grid supply failed on 9 August.
Western Power Distribution reconnected customers before being instructed by the ESO.
The ESO first contacted Ofgem at 18:00 BST.
The ESO first contacted BEIS at 17:00 BST.
The late ESO communications caused the demand disconnection to last longer and prolonged the outage.
Under ESQCR and Grid Code OC7 the DNOs had to report the incident to the ESO within an hour.
GTR's fleet log S09-GTR-42 shows that 40 trains needed a technician.

report.executive_summary: The Blyth–Eccles–Stella West trip at 16:50:44 started the event [X01]. The ESO's Table 2 total is 1,990 MW [X02]; Ofgem reports 931 MW of LFDD disconnection and the DNOs 892 MW [X03, X04]. Distributed generation lost on loss-of-mains protection totalled 1,462 MW, and overall 2,628 MW of generation was lost [X05, X06]. Secondary response held was 1,338 MW per Table 3 and inertia 219,632 MVA.s per Table 4 [X07, X08]. A faulty speed sensor and a failed bypass valve caused the Little Barford trips; GT1B tripped automatically (S07-E14) [X09, X10]. The DRC caused the Hornsea de-load [X11]. Frequency fell to 49.1 Hz and then 48.8 Hz and was below 49 Hz for 40 s [X12, X13, X14]. Demand was restored at 18:34 [X15]. On the railway 29 trains locked out, 27 reset by drivers and 30 by technicians [X18]; the Class 387s shut down too and the traction supply was lost [X19, X21]. Newcastle Airport tripped on its own protection and Ipswich Hospital was cut by LFDD [X24, X32]. The ESO contacted Ofgem at 18:00 [X27]. Late communications prolonged the outage [X29]. It is established that the root cause was a faulty speed sensor [X09]. In January 2020 RWE and Ørsted paid £4.5m each into the redress scheme [X16].

sections.body: 1. Ofgem should fine the generators again [X16, X17].
